title: A crowded nav runs off screen above 48rem with no way to reach it
foundBy: session agent, probing Header with many nav items after the report behind CUI-080
details:
`flex-wrap: wrap` on the nav link row exists only inside `@media (max-width: 48rem)` in `src/styles/components/app-shell.css`. Above that breakpoint the row is `nowrap`, and `src/components/AppShell.responsive.test.tsx` asserts that at 1440 pixels wide.

So a header with many nav items has no handling at desktop widths. Measured at 8ada6d1 with 20 items: at 1000 pixels wide, 7 links sit past the right edge of the viewport, and at 1440 pixels wide, 1 does.

Those links cannot be reached. `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` equals the viewport width in both cases, so no horizontal scrollbar appears. The shell root sets `overflow: hidden`, which clips them instead of scrolling to them.

A nav destination that renders but cannot be clicked or tabbed to is worse than one that is absent, because nothing tells the reader it is there.

Moving the one `flex-wrap` declaration out of the media query would fix the unreachability without a new prop or a new component. The cost is a taller header when the nav is crowded.

notes.text: Measured with markup replicated from `src/components/AppShell.tsx` and the real stylesheets, not with the rendered component. Confirm against the rendered `Header` before closing this.
